questions.question: The normal value of prothrombin time (PT) is:
questions.explanation: PT assesses the extrinsic pathway and is normally 11-15 seconds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal value of partial thromboplastin time (PTT) is:
questions.explanation: PTT assesses the intrinsic pathway and heparin therapy; normal is about 25-40 seconds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An INR ratio of more than ______ increases the risk of haemarthrosis.
questions.explanation: Over-anticoagulation (INR above about 3) raises the risk of spontaneous bleeding into joints.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In normal individuals total serum cholesterol should be less than ______ mg/dL.
questions.explanation: Desirable total cholesterol is below 200 mg/dL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In normal individuals LDL cholesterol should be less than ______ mg/dL.
questions.explanation: Optimal LDL is below 100 mg/dL (below 70 in high-risk patients).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In normal individuals HDL cholesterol should be more than about ______ mg/dL.
questions.explanation: HDL below 40 mg/dL is a risk factor; above 60 is protective.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In which zone of a myocardial infarct is there death of cells (necrosis)?
questions.explanation: The infarcted central zone is necrotic; around it lie the zones of injury and ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The skin, the largest organ of the body, comprises about ______ percent of body weight.
questions.explanation: Skin forms roughly 15 percent of adult body weight.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Herpes zoster (shingles) is caused by:
questions.explanation: Reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus in a dorsal root ganglion causes shingles.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)?

options.B: A typical butterfly rash across the bridge of the nose is seen

questions.explanation: SLE is a chronic autoimmune disease with remissions and relapses but no cure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following clinical manifestations is FALSE regarding malignant melanoma?

options.B: The diameter of the lesion is less than 6 mm
options.C: The commonest type is superficial spreading melanoma
options.D: The colour of the lesion is red, blue or black

questions.explanation: The ABCDE rule: asymmetry, border irregularity, colour variation, diameter above 6 mm and evolving.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE for an arterial ulcer?

options.A: The common site is the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: Arterial ulcers hurt more on elevation; dependency relieves the pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE for a venous ulcer?

options.B: The temperature of the affected part is low

questions.explanation: A venous ulcer limb is usually warm, with oedema and good granulation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A pressure ulcer that presents as a deep crater (full-thickness skin loss) is:
questions.explanation: Stage 3: full-thickness loss with visible subcutaneous fat but no muscle or bone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A pressure ulcer that presents as a shallow crater or blister (partial thickness) is:
questions.explanation: Stage 2: partial-thickness loss of epidermis and part of the dermis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A pressure ulcer that shows involvement of sinus tracts is:
questions.explanation: Stage 4: full-thickness loss with exposed muscle, tendon or bone and often sinus tracts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Partial-thickness skin loss involving the epidermis and part of the dermis is seen in:
questions.explanation: Stage 2 ulcers are shallow open lesions with a red-pink bed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Full-thickness loss with direct visibility of tendon, bone and muscle is:
questions.explanation: Stage 4 exposes deep structures.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Wagner ulcer classification, an ulcer with gangrene of a digit (forefoot) is grade:
questions.explanation: Wagner 4 is localised gangrene of the toes or forefoot.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Wagner classification, gangrene of the whole foot is grade:
questions.explanation: Wagner 5 requires major amputation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Wagner classification, a superficial ulcer without involvement of subcutaneous tissue is grade:
questions.explanation: Grade 0: no open lesion; grade 1: superficial ulcer.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Wagner classification, a deep ulcer with osteomyelitis or abscess is grade:
questions.explanation: Wagner 3: deep ulcer with abscess or osteomyelitis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sanguineous wound exudate contains:
questions.explanation: Sanguineous exudate is bloody, seen with vascular damage.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Serous exudate is usually:
questions.explanation: Serous exudate is thin and watery.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Serosanguineous exudate is usually:
questions.explanation: It is blood-tinged serous fluid.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Seropurulent exudate is usually:
questions.explanation: Seropurulent contains serous fluid and pus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Purulent exudate is usually:
questions.explanation: Purulent exudate is thick pus and indicates infection.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a route of transmission of HIV?

options.B: Unprotected sexual contact with an infected person
options.C: Transmission from mother to child in utero

questions.explanation: HIV is not spread by air; casual contact does not transmit it.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The transmission mode of hepatitis A is:
questions.explanation: Hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food and water.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The transmission mode of hepatitis B is:

options.A: Body fluids, sexual contact and contaminated needles

questions.explanation: Hepatitis B is a blood-borne virus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In order to sterilise instruments, the autoclave temperature should be set at about:
questions.explanation: Steam autoclaving at 121 C (250 F) for 15-20 minutes sterilises instruments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can cause a hypercoagulability disorder?

options.B: All of these: use of oral contraceptive pills, immobility and elevated lipids

questions.explanation: Stasis, vessel injury and hypercoagulable states form Virchow's triad.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can cause a hypocoagulability disorder?

options.B: All of these: haemophilia, thrombocytopenia and von Willebrand's disease

questions.explanation: These are bleeding disorders.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Instead of the normal biconcave shape, the RBC changes to a crescent shape in:
questions.explanation: HbS polymerises in deoxygenated conditions, sickling the cell.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In haemophilia A there is a deficiency of clotting factor:
questions.explanation: Haemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency; haemophilia B (Christmas disease) is factor IX deficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Christmas disease (haemophilia B) there is a deficiency of clotting factor:
questions.explanation: Factor IX deficiency causes haemophilia B.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
